pathogen_scientific_name.quote: Sugarcane yellow leaf virus (SCYLV) is a distinct member of the Polerovirus genus of the Luteoviridae family

type_of_disease.quote: Sugarcane yellow leaf virus (SCYLV) is a distinct member of the Polerovirus genus of the Luteoviridae family

affected_parts.quote: The YLD affected sugarcane plants exhibited various symptoms including mild to severe yellowing of the midribs, smaller and clustering of leaves at the crown region of the plant along with the shortened internodes. Midrib yellowing, necrosis observed from tip to the base of leaves. Subsequently, complete drying of leaf foliage

summary.value: Mild to severe yellowing of midribs in both young and mature leaves, progressing to leaf necrosis, complete leaf drying, stunting and poor plant growth in severe cases.
summary.quote: The YLD affected sugarcane plants exhibited various symptoms including mild to severe yellowing of the midribs...smaller and clustering of leaves at the crown region of the plant along with the shortened internodes. Midrib yellowing...necrosis observed from tip to the base of leaves. Subsequently, complete drying of leaf foliage with stunted and poor growth

diagnostic_features.value: Yellowing specifically of the midribs (leaf veins), necrosis progressing from leaf tip to base, clustering of leaves at the crown, shortened internodes, and in severe cases, complete drying and stunting
diagnostic_features.quote: mild to severe yellowing of the midribs...Midrib yellowing...necrosis observed from tip to the base of leaves...smaller and clustering of leaves at the crown region of the plant along with the shortened internodes

look_alikes.quote: sugarcane is infected by different virus species viz., Sugarcane yellow leaf virus (SCYLV) inducing yellow leaf disease (YLD), Sugarcane streak virus (SSV) responsible for causing streak disease, Sugarcane Fiji disease virus (SFDV) causing infamous Fiji disease, Sugarcane bacilliform virus (SCBV) known to induce fleck leaf disease...and Sugarcane streak mosaic virus (SCSMV), and Sugarcane mosaic virus (SCMV)...are associated with mosaic disease

pathogen_scientific_name.quote: The causal agent of sugarcane mosaic was originally named Marmor sacchari and was renamed sugarcane mosaic virus (SCMV) in the early 1970s

type_of_disease.quote: Mosaic is one of the main viral sugarcane diseases.

affected_parts.quote: In infected sugarcane plants, chlorophyll is destroyed, photosynthesis is weakened, and growth is significantly inhibited, resulting in shorter internodes, fewer mill-able stems, shorter roots. Systemic infection is caused by the virus after it invades sugarcane. They move quickly in vascular bundles, along with the flow of plant nutrients. As a result, the virus can spread to almost every tissue, even the whole stool.

summary.value: Leaves exhibit irregular yellow and green mosaic patterns (inlays, stripes, and mottles) alternating with parallel veins, clearly visible against sunlight. Severely infected leaves turn yellow or yellow-white with red punctate necrosis or abnormally twisted tips. Large yellow or light green areas without small streaks are also characteristic.
summary.quote: In comparison to healthy leaves, there are many irregular yellow and green inlays, stripes, or mottles alternate with parallel veins on symptomatic leaves, more clearly visible against the sunlight. Some show very obvious whole leaf chlorosis, and the seriously infected leaves turn yellow or yellow white, leaving only a few green islets or a small amount of red punctate necrosis, or the tips of new leaves are abnormally twisted.

diagnostic_features.value: Yellow and green mosaic pattern (inlays, stripes, and mottles) alternating with parallel veins on symptomatic leaves, distinctly visible against sunlight; large yellow or light green areas without small streaks (distinguishing from SCSMV which shows numerous small streaks).
diagnostic_features.quote: there are many irregular yellow and green inlays, stripes, or mottles alternate with parallel veins on symptomatic leaves, more clearly visible against the sunlight.

look_alikes.quote: In sugarcane, mosaic-type symptoms such as green, white, or yellow areas, spots, streaks, and stripes can be caused by at least seven viruses: SCMV, SrMV, SCSMV, maize yellow mosaic virus, sugarcane mild mosaic virus, sugarcane striate mosaic associated virus, and maize striate mosaic virus

conflicts.alternative_value: Also caused by Sorghum mosaic virus (SrMV) and/or Sugarcane streak mosaic virus (SCSMV) in compound infections
conflicts.note: PMC source notes mosaic disease can be caused by single or compound infection of SCMV, SrMV, and/or SCSMV; APS source attributes mosaic primarily to SCMV or SrMV

conflicts.canonical_value: Foliar, Stem, Root, Vascular, Whole plant
conflicts.note: APS journal source mentions only foliar symptoms; PMC source describes systemic infection spreading to all tissues

pathogen_scientific_name.quote: Sugarcane streak mosaic virus (SCSMV), now assigned to the genus Poacevirus of the family Potyviridae

affected_parts.quote: Symptoms of streak mosaic caused by SCSMV are patterns of green color on the leaf lamina... symptoms are usually easy to recognize on the spindle leaves and the top visible dewlap leaf of 3- to 6-month-old plants

summary.value: Patterns of green color on leaf lamina with longitudinal, yellow-green interveinal streaks (3 to 40 mm long) and light and dark green islands.
summary.quote: Symptoms of streak mosaic caused by SCSMV are patterns of green color on the leaf lamina, which include longitudinal, yellow-green interveinal streaks (3 to 40 mm long) and light and dark green islands

diagnostic_features.value: Numerous streaks of various sizes on leaves, unlike SCMV which shows large areas without small streaks.
diagnostic_features.quote: leaves infected by SCMV often show large yellow or light green areas without small streaks, whereas leaves infected by SCSMV show numerous streaks of various sizes

look_alikes.quote: In sugarcane, mosaic-type symptoms such as green, white, or yellow areas, spots, streaks, and stripes can be caused by at least seven viruses: SCMV, SrMV, SCSMV, maize yellow mosaic virus, sugarcane mild mosaic virus, sugarcane striate mosaic associated virus, and maize striate mosaic virus

pathogen_scientific_name.quote: The disease is caused by a phytoplasma.

affected_parts.quote: Leaves become pale yellow to completely chlorotic, thin and narrow... The disease is characterised by the production of numerous lanky tillers from the base of the affected shoots... Two types of bodies are seen in ultrathin sections of phloem cells of infected plants... The affected clumps are stunted

summary.value: Plants exhibit numerous lanky tillers from the base with pale yellow to completely chlorotic, thin and narrow leaves, appearing bushy and grass-like due to reduced internode length and premature continuous tillering.
summary.quote: The disease is characterised by the production of numerous lanky tillers from the base of the affected shoots. Leaves become pale yellow to completely chlorotic, thin and narrow. The plants appear bushy and 'grass-like' due to reduction in the length of internodes premature and continuous tillering.

diagnostic_features.value: Grass-like bushy appearance with severely reduced internode length, premature and continuous tillering from plant base, chlorotic thin narrow leaves, stunted clumps with papery abnormally elongated buds on canes, aerial roots at lower nodes.
diagnostic_features.quote: The plants appear bushy and 'grass-like' due to reduction in the length of internodes premature and continuous tillering... The affected clumps are stunted with premature proliferation of auxillary buds... if formed, thin with shorter internodes having aerial roots at the lower nodes. The buds on such canes usually papery and abnormally elongated.

pathogen_scientific_name.quote: brown spot caused by Cercospora longipes E.J. Butler in parts of Karnataka and Maharashtra

affected_parts.quote: The foliar diseases like eye spot, brown spot, rust and others in sugarcane

pathogen_scientific_name.quote: the bacterium Xanthomonas albilineans causes leaf scald

type_of_disease.quote: the bacterium Xanthomonas albilineans causes leaf scald

affected_parts.quote: The most common symptom of leaf scald is a white line about 1–2 mm wide (also called a pencil line) on the leaf.

summary.value: Leaf scald presents as a white pencil line on leaves extending from the midrib to the margin with a diffuse yellow border, progressing to brown dead tissue that causes leaves to look burned and curl inward.
summary.quote: The most common symptom of leaf scald is a white line about 1–2 mm wide (also called a pencil line) on the leaf. This line extends from the midrib to the leaf margin running parallel to the veins. A diffuse yellow border of varying widths runs parallel to the pencil line.

diagnostic_features.value: White pencil line (1-2 mm wide) extending from midrib to leaf margin parallel to veins, diffuse yellow border, reddish discoloration along the pencil line, and brown necrosis developing from leaf tip or margin creating a scalded appearance.
diagnostic_features.quote: This line extends from the midrib to the leaf margin running parallel to the veins. A diffuse yellow border of varying widths runs parallel to the pencil line. The pencil line may have areas of reddish discoloration along part of its length. As the disease progresses, brown, dead tissue (necrosis) develops from the leaf tip or leaf margin and eventually extends the entire leaf.

pathogen_scientific_name.quote: Sett rot or Pineapple disease - Ceratocystis paradoxa

type_of_disease.quote: The fungus is soil-borne and enters through cut ends and proliferates rapidly in the parenchymatous tissues.

affected_parts.quote: The disease primarily affects the setts usually two to three weeks after planning... The setts may decay before the buds germinate or the shoots may die after reaching a height of about 6-12 inches. Infected shoots are stunted.

summary.value: Affected tissues develop a reddish colour turning brownish black in later stages, with internodal cavities covered by mycelium and spores, accompanied by a characteristic pineapple smell.
summary.quote: The affected tissues first develop a reddish colour which turns to brownish black in the later stages. The severely affected setts show internodal cavities covered with the mycelium and abundant spores. A characteristic pineapple smell is associated with the rotting tissues.

diagnostic_features.value: Characteristic pineapple smell associated with rotting tissues and internodal cavities covered with mycelium and abundant spores.
diagnostic_features.quote: A characteristic pineapple smell is associated with the rotting tissues. The severely affected setts show internodal cavities covered with the mycelium and abundant spores.

pathogen_scientific_name.value: Fusarium species complex (Fusarium sacchari, Fusarium proliferatum, Fusarium verticillioides)
pathogen_scientific_name.quote: It is caused by the Fusarium species complex ( Fusarium sacchari, Fusarium proliferatum, Fusarium verticillioides etc.,).

affected_parts.quote: Chlorotic, rough, wrinkling, twisting and shortening of the leaves... Knife cut phase (Its look like the tissues of the stem are removed with a sharp knife). Shortening of internodes.

summary.value: Disease exhibits multiple phases: chlorotic phase with rough, wrinkled, twisted, and shortened leaves; top rot phase where the growing point is killed and the entire top of the plant dies; and knife cut phase with characteristic stem damage.
summary.quote: Chlorotic phase (chlorotic, rough, wrinkling, twisting and shortening of the leaves). Top rot phase (growing point is killed and the entire top of the plant dies). Knife cut phase (Its look like the tissues of the stem are removed with a sharp knife).

diagnostic_features.value: The knife cut phase produces characteristic stem damage appearing as if tissues were removed with a sharp knife, distinguishing it from other diseases.
diagnostic_features.quote: Knife cut phase (Its look like the tissues of the stem are removed with a sharp knife).
